options.D: It must always be a single column

questions.question: Differentiate between DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP.
questions.model_answer: DELETE (DML) removes chosen rows using WHERE and can be rolled back. TRUNCATE removes all rows quickly, resets identity counters and cannot take a WHERE clause. DROP removes the entire table definition together with its data and indexes.

questions.question: What is the difference between a primary key, a unique key and a foreign key?
questions.model_answer: Primary key: unique and NOT NULL, one per table. Unique key: unique values, may allow NULL, many per table. Foreign key: column(s) that reference a key of another table to enforce referential integrity.

questions.question: Explain 1NF, 2NF and 3NF in one line each.
questions.model_answer: 1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups. 2NF: 1NF plus no partial dependency of non-key columns on part of a composite key. 3NF: 2NF plus no transitive dependency (non-key column depending on another non-key column).

questions.question: Explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING with an example.
questions.model_answer: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping and cannot use aggregates. HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Example: WHERE salary > 50000 removes rows first; HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 keeps only groups with more than three rows.

questions.question: Differentiate super key, candidate key and composite key.
questions.model_answer: Super key: any set of columns that uniquely identifies a row. Candidate key: a minimal super key. Composite key: a key made of two or more columns. One candidate key is chosen as the primary key.

questions.question: What is an index? Explain clustered vs non-clustered.
questions.model_answer: An index is a separate structure (usually a B-tree) that speeds up lookups at the cost of extra storage and slower writes. A clustered index defines the physical order of rows (one per table); a non-clustered index stores key values with pointers to the rows (many per table).

questions.question: What is a view and can you update data through it?
questions.model_answer: A view is a stored SELECT that behaves like a virtual table. Simple views over a single table without aggregates, DISTINCT or joins are usually updatable; complex views generally are not.

questions.question: When would you intentionally denormalize a database?
questions.model_answer: For read-heavy reporting or analytics workloads where joins are expensive: storing precomputed or duplicated columns trades storage and update complexity for faster reads.

questions.question: Compare a subquery with a join. When would you prefer each?

questions.question: How would you find and remove duplicate rows from a table that has no unique key?

To delete, keep one row per group using ROW_NUMBER() over the business columns (delete rn > 1) or, if a surrogate id exists, delete ids not in (SELECT MIN(id) ... GROUP BY business columns). Finally add a UNIQUE constraint to prevent recurrence.

questions.question: A report query is slow. List the first five things you would check.
questions.model_answer: 1) Execution plan (full scans, bad join order). 2) Missing or unusable indexes (functions on indexed columns, leading wildcards). 3) Selecting unnecessary columns or rows. 4) Row-by-row subqueries that can become joins. 5) Stale statistics, data volume and locking or blocking.

questions.question: What is the difference between IN and EXISTS?
questions.model_answer: IN compares a value against a list or subquery result set; EXISTS checks whether a correlated subquery returns any row and stops at the first match. EXISTS handles NULLs more safely than NOT IN.

questions.question: Why can NOT IN return no rows when the subquery contains a NULL?
questions.model_answer: x NOT IN (a, NULL) evaluates to UNKNOWN for every x that is not equal to a, so no row qualifies. Use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs out of the subquery.

questions.question: Explain how an index improves query performance and when it can hurt.
questions.model_answer: An index (typically a B-tree) lets the engine seek to matching rows instead of scanning the table. It hurts when the table is write-heavy (every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must also maintain the index), when the column has very low selectivity, or when the query wraps the indexed column in a function, which prevents index use.

questions.question: What is the difference between 3NF and BCNF?
questions.model_answer: 3NF allows a non-key attribute to determine a prime attribute; BCNF is stricter and requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key. Every BCNF relation is in 3NF but not vice versa.

questions.question: OLTP vs OLAP: what is the difference?
questions.model_answer: OLTP handles many short read/write transactions on normalised data (orders, payments). OLAP handles large read-heavy analytical queries over denormalised, historical data (star or snowflake schemas) with aggregations.

questions.question: CTE vs subquery vs temporary table: when do you use which?
questions.model_answer: A CTE names a subquery for readability and enables recursion; a subquery is fine for one-off filters; a temporary table is materialised and indexed, so it suits reuse across many statements or very large intermediate results.

questions.question: What is a star schema?
questions.model_answer: A warehouse design with a central fact table (measures such as sales amount) surrounded by denormalised dimension tables (date, product, customer, region) joined by foreign keys. It makes analytical queries simple and fast.

questions.question: What is ETL and where does SQL fit in?

questions.question: Build the points table: 2 points per win, 1 point for each no-result match, 0 for a loss. Show team, matches played, wins, points, ordered by points then wins.

questions.question: Explain ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK with a tie example.
questions.model_answer: With salaries 300, 200, 200, 100: ROW_NUMBER gives 1,2,3,4 (arbitrary among ties); RANK gives 1,2,2,4 (gap after ties); DENSE_RANK gives 1,2,2,3 (no gaps). Use ROW_NUMBER to pick exactly one row per group, DENSE_RANK for Nth-highest value problems.

questions.question: What is the difference between ROWS and RANGE in a window frame?
questions.model_answer: ROWS counts physical rows relative to the current row (e.g. 6 PRECEDING = previous six rows). RANGE works on the ORDER BY value, so peers with equal values are included together. The default frame with ORDER BY is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, which surprises people with tied values.

questions.question: Describe nested loop, hash and merge joins and when each wins.
questions.model_answer: Nested loop: best when one side is small or an index lookup is available. Hash join: builds a hash table on the smaller input; best for large unsorted equi-joins. Merge join: needs both inputs sorted on the join key; best when already sorted or indexed.

questions.question: Find the top 3 best-selling products (by units) in every category, keeping ties.

questions.question: For each customer show the first order's id, date and total value.

questions.question: Find the 5 most frequent pairs of products that were bought together in the same order.

questions.question: Find customers whose second order was worth more than their first order (show both values).

questions.question: What share of total delivered revenue comes from the top 10 percent of customers (the first decile by spend)?

questions.question: What is a deadlock in a database and how can it be reduced?
questions.model_answer: A deadlock occurs when two transactions each hold a lock the other needs, so neither can proceed; the engine kills one as the victim. Reduce them by accessing tables in a consistent order, keeping transactions short, using appropriate indexes and lower isolation levels, and retrying on deadlock errors.

questions.question: What does SARGable mean and why does it matter?
questions.model_answer: A predicate is SARGable (Search ARGument ABLE) when the engine can use an index seek for it. WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' is SARGable; WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2024 is not, because the function on the column forces a scan. Rewrite predicates so the column stays bare.

questions.question: View vs CTE: what is the difference?
questions.model_answer: A view is a stored object in the database that can be reused by many queries and permissions can be granted on it. A CTE exists only for the duration of one statement and is mainly for readability or recursion.

questions.question: State the logical order in which a SELECT query is evaluated.
questions.model_answer: FROM / JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, window functions, SELECT (projection and aliases), DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET. This explains why a column alias cannot be used in WHERE but can be used in ORDER BY.

questions.question: A join returns more rows than expected. How do you diagnose it?
questions.model_answer: The usual cause is row fan-out from a one-to-many or many-to-many join key. Check key uniqueness with GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 on each side, compare COUNT(*) before and after the join, and aggregate or deduplicate one side before joining.

questions.question: How do you write a NULL-safe equality comparison?
questions.model_answer: ANSI SQL: a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b (PostgreSQL, SQL Server 2022). MySQL: a <=> b. Portable fallback: (a = b OR (a IS NULL AND b IS NULL)).

questions.question: For every login date, count the distinct users who logged in during that day and the 6 days before it (rolling 7-day active users).
questions.solution_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT login_date FROM logins) SELECT d.login_date, COUNT(DISTINCT l.user_id) AS rolling_7d_users FROM d JOIN logins l ON DATEDIFF(d.login_date, l.login_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 6 GROUP BY d.login_date ORDER BY d.login_date

questions.question: Compute the median salary of each department.
questions.solution_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT dept_id, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id) AS n FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS median_salary FROM r WHERE rn >= n / 2.0 AND rn <= n / 2.0 + 1 GROUP BY dept_id

questions.question: Find the manager with the largest total team size, counting direct and indirect reports.
questions.solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT manager_id AS boss, emp_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT t.boss, e.emp_id FROM t JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = t.emp_id) SELECT m.emp_name, COUNT(*) AS team_size FROM t JOIN employees m ON m.emp_id = t.boss GROUP BY t.boss, m.emp_name ORDER BY team_size DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: List employees whose salary is within 10 percent of the highest salary in their department.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_name, dept_id, salary FROM (SELECT emp_name, dept_id, salary, MAX(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id) AS dept_max FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL) t WHERE salary >= 0.9 * dept_max

questions.question: For each user, show the date of their 3rd login in the data, skipping users with fewer than 3 logins.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT user_id, login_date AS third_login FROM (SELECT user_id, login_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn FROM logins) t WHERE rn = 3

questions.question: Find players who scored 50 or more runs in at least 3 matches.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.player_name, COUNT(*) AS fifties FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id WHERE pp.runs >= 50 GROUP BY pl.player_id, pl.player_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY fifties DESC

questions.question: List the top 5 batters by strike rate (runs x 100 / balls), only for players who faced at least 100 balls in total.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.player_name, SUM(pp.runs) AS runs, SUM(pp.balls) AS balls, ROUND(SUM(pp.runs) * 100.0 / SUM(pp.balls), 2) AS strike_rate FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id GROUP BY pl.player_id, pl.player_name HAVING SUM(pp.balls) >= 100 ORDER BY strike_rate DESC LIMIT 5

questions.question: Find the leading run scorer of every team (team name, player and total runs), keeping ties.
questions.solution_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT tm.team_name, pl.player_name, SUM(pp.runs) AS runs FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id JOIN teams tm ON pl.team_id = tm.team_id GROUP BY tm.team_id, tm.team_name, pl.player_id, pl.player_name) SELECT team_name, player_name, runs FROM (SELECT team_name, player_name, runs, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY team_name ORDER BY runs DESC) AS rnk FROM t) x WHERE rnk = 1

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: List matches in which the best individual score of the winning team was lower than the best individual score of the losing team (ignore no-result matches).
questions.solution_sql: WITH best AS (SELECT pp.match_id, pl.team_id, MAX(pp.runs) AS top_score FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id GROUP BY pp.match_id, pl.team_id) SELECT m.match_id, m.winner_id, w.top_score AS winner_top, l.top_score AS loser_top FROM matches m JOIN best w ON w.match_id = m.match_id AND w.team_id = m.winner_id JOIN best l ON l.match_id = m.match_id AND l.team_id = CASE WHEN m.winner_id = m.team1_id THEN m.team2_id ELSE m.team1_id END WHERE m.winner_id IS NOT NULL AND w.top_score < l.top_score

questions.question: Offset pagination gets slower on deep pages. What is the alternative?
questions.model_answer: Keyset (seek) pagination: remember the last seen sort key and query WHERE (created_at, id) < (:last_created_at, :last_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n. It uses an index seek instead of scanning and discarding OFFSET rows.

questions.question: How would you avoid overselling stock during a flash sale at the database level?
questions.model_answer: Use an atomic conditional update (UPDATE inventory SET qty = qty - 1 WHERE sku = ? AND qty > 0 and check rows affected), or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a short transaction, or optimistic locking with a version column. Keep the transaction short and index the sku column.

questions.question: For each category show how many items were sold at a discount (unit_price below list price) and the average discount percentage on those items.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) AS discounted_items, ROUND(AVG((p.price - oi.unit_price) * 100.0 / p.price), 2) AS avg_discount_pct FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.unit_price < p.price GROUP BY p.category

questions.question: Calculate the revenue given away as discounts, ((list price - unit_price) x quantity), for every brand, highest first.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.brand, SUM((p.price - oi.unit_price) * oi.quantity) AS discount_value FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.brand ORDER BY discount_value DESC

questions.question: Compare the cancellation-plus-return percentage of Cash-on-Delivery orders against all prepaid orders (two rows: COD and Prepaid).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN payment_mode = 'COD' THEN 'COD' ELSE 'Prepaid' END AS mode_type, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS bad_order_pct FROM orders GROUP BY CASE WHEN payment_mode = 'COD' THEN 'COD' ELSE 'Prepaid' END

questions.question: Show the top 2 customers by delivered spend in every state.
questions.solution_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.state, c.customer_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.state, c.customer_name) SELECT state, customer_name, spend FROM (SELECT state, customer_name, spend, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY spend DESC) AS rn FROM s) t WHERE rn <= 2

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: List products that had no sale in June 2024.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2024-06-01' AND '2024-06-30')

questions.question: Within each category show every brand's share (percentage) of that category's revenue.
questions.solution_sql: WITH b AS (SELECT p.category, p.brand, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category, p.brand) SELECT category, brand, revenue, ROUND(revenue * 100.0 / SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 2) AS category_share_pct FROM b ORDER BY category, revenue DESC

questions.question: Rank products within their category by revenue and show how far each product's revenue is from the category leader.
questions.solution_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category, p.product_name) SELECT category, product_name, revenue, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk, MAX(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category) - revenue AS gap_to_leader FROM r ORDER BY category, rnk

questions.question: Find the average number of days between a customer's signup and their first order (customers with orders only).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF(f.first_order, c.signup_date)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_order FROM customers c JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_order FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) f ON c.customer_id = f.customer_id

questions.question: Show the number of orders placed on weekends (Saturday and Sunday) versus weekdays (MySQL DAYOFWEEK: 1 = Sunday, 7 = Saturday).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_date) IN (1, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_date) IN (1, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END

questions.question: List cities whose total delivered revenue is above the average city revenue.
questions.solution_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers cu ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY cu.city) SELECT city, revenue FROM c WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM c)

questions.question: For every customer find their second most frequently purchased category (by number of items); skip customers with only one category.
questions.solution_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.customer_id, p.category, COUNT(*) AS items FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, p.category) SELECT customer_id, category, items FROM (SELECT customer_id, category, items, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY items DESC, category) AS rn FROM c) t WHERE rn = 2

questions.question: Show every customer's most recent order with its status and date.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date, status FROM (SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date, status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, order_id DESC) AS rn FROM orders) t WHERE rn = 1

questions.question: Find customers all of whose orders were delivered (none cancelled, returned or still shipped) and who have at least 3 orders.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 AND SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'Delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0

questions.question: Show cumulative monthly delivered revenue for each category (running total within the category).
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT p.category, DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY p.category, DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m')) SELECT category, ym, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY ym) AS cumulative_revenue FROM m ORDER BY category, ym

questions.question: For each month show what percentage of orders were paid by UPI.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN payment_mode = 'UPI' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS upi_pct FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(order_date, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY ym

questions.question: Find products whose current stock is less than twice the total units ever sold (a restocking alert).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.product_name, p.stock, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS units_sold FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, p.stock HAVING p.stock < 2 * COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)

questions.question: For each category show the percentage of reviews that are positive (rating 4 or 5).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN r.rating >= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS positive_pct FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category

questions.question: Reduce the list price by 5 percent for every product that has never been sold.
questions.solution_sql: UPDATE products SET price = price * 0.95 WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM order_items)

questions.question: Delete all cancelled orders together with their order items (write the statements in a safe order).
questions.solution_sql: DELETE FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'Cancelled'); DELETE FROM orders WHERE status = 'Cancelled'

questions.question: Find customers who ordered in two consecutive calendar months at least once.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, YEAR(order_date) * 12 + MONTH(order_date) AS mi FROM orders) SELECT DISTINCT a.customer_id FROM m a JOIN m b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id AND b.mi = a.mi + 1

questions.question: Explain optimistic versus pessimistic locking.
questions.model_answer: Pessimistic locking acquires locks up front (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), preventing conflicts but reducing concurrency. Optimistic locking lets transactions proceed and checks at commit that nothing changed (version or timestamp column); on conflict the transaction is retried. Optimistic suits low-contention workloads.

questions.question: What is the difference between partitioning and sharding?
questions.model_answer: Partitioning splits a large table into pieces inside one database instance (by range, list or hash) to speed up pruning and maintenance. Sharding spreads data across multiple database servers, each owning a subset, to scale writes and storage horizontally.

questions.question: How would you optimise a query that joins two tables with hundreds of millions of rows?
questions.model_answer: Filter early and select only needed columns; index the join and filter keys; check the plan for the join strategy; pre-aggregate one side; partition by date to prune; avoid functions on join columns; consider materialised summaries; and update statistics.

questions.question: Show each product's stock value (price x stock) and rank products by it within their category.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT category, product_name, price * stock AS stock_value, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price * stock DESC) AS rnk FROM products ORDER BY category, rnk

questions.question: Compute a sell-through ratio (units sold divided by units sold plus current stock) for each product, and list the 5 products with the highest ratio.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS units_sold, p.stock, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) * 1.0 / (COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) + p.stock + 0.0001), 4) AS sell_through FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, p.stock ORDER BY sell_through DESC LIMIT 5

questions.question: Show each customer's delivered spend on Electronics and on Fashion as two columns.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(CASE WHEN p.category = 'Electronics' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS electronics_spend, SUM(CASE WHEN p.category = 'Fashion' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS fashion_spend FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id

questions.question: For each city find the customer(s) with the highest number of orders.
questions.solution_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.city, cu.customer_name, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders o JOIN customers cu ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.city, cu.customer_name) SELECT city, customer_name, orders FROM (SELECT city, customer_name, orders, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY orders DESC) AS rnk FROM c) t WHERE rnk = 1

questions.question: Build one activity feed per customer combining orders (activity 'ORDER') and reviews (activity 'REVIEW'), sorted by customer and date.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, order_date AS activity_date, 'ORDER' AS activity FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT customer_id, review_date, 'REVIEW' FROM reviews ORDER BY customer_id, activity_date

questions.question: Rewrite this query using a JOIN instead of IN: SELECT emp_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id IN (SELECT dept_id FROM departments WHERE location = 'Bengaluru').
questions.solution_sql: SELECT e.emp_name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id WHERE d.location = 'Bengaluru'

questions.question: For each account show successful transactions in date order with a running balance of net movement (credits positive, debits negative).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT account_id, txn_id, txn_date, txn_type, amount, SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'CREDIT' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date, txn_id) AS running_net FROM transactions WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY account_id, txn_date, txn_id

questions.question: Find the account with the highest net inflow (credits minus debits, successful only) in the quarter April to June 2024.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'CREDIT' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net_inflow FROM transactions WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' AND txn_date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-06-30' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY net_inflow DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Delete duplicate payments that share the same user, merchant, date and amount, keeping the one with the lowest payment_id.
questions.solution_sql: DELETE FROM payments WHERE payment_id IN (SELECT payment_id FROM (SELECT payment_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, merchant_id, pay_date, amount ORDER BY payment_id) AS rn FROM payments) t WHERE rn > 1)

questions.question: Write a transaction that moves 5000 from account 1 to account 2 and rolls back if the debit would make the balance negative (MySQL-style pseudocode with ROLLBACK).
questions.solution_sql: START TRANSACTION; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 5000 WHERE account_id = 1 AND balance >= 5000; -- check ROW_COUNT() = 1, else ROLLBACK; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 5000 WHERE account_id = 2; COMMIT;

questions.question: For every restaurant city show the total orders, delivered orders and GMV (order_value minus discount for delivered orders).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT r.city, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(CASE WHEN f.status = 'Delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered, SUM(CASE WHEN f.status = 'Delivered' THEN f.order_value - f.discount ELSE 0 END) AS gmv FROM food_orders f JOIN restaurants r ON f.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.city

questions.question: Find the 5 restaurants with the highest cancellation rate (percentage of cancelled orders), showing the rate.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT r.restaurant_name, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN f.status = 'Cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancel_rate_pct FROM food_orders f JOIN restaurants r ON f.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.restaurant_name ORDER BY cancel_rate_pct DESC, orders DESC LIMIT 5

questions.question: List riders whose average delivery time is slower than the overall average delivery time.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rd.rider_name, ROUND(AVG(f.delivery_minutes), 1) AS avg_minutes FROM food_orders f JOIN riders rd ON f.rider_id = rd.rider_id WHERE f.delivery_minutes IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rd.rider_id, rd.rider_name HAVING AVG(f.delivery_minutes) > (SELECT AVG(delivery_minutes) FROM food_orders)

questions.question: Show the number of orders placed in each hour of the day and identify the busiest hour.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT HOUR(order_ts) AS hr, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM food_orders GROUP BY HOUR(order_ts) ORDER BY orders DESC

questions.question: Within each cuisine, list the top 3 restaurants by GMV (delivered orders), keeping ties.
questions.solution_sql: WITH g AS (SELECT r.cuisine, r.restaurant_name, SUM(f.order_value - f.discount) AS gmv FROM food_orders f JOIN restaurants r ON f.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id WHERE f.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.cuisine, r.restaurant_name) SELECT cuisine, restaurant_name, gmv FROM (SELECT cuisine, restaurant_name, gmv, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cuisine ORDER BY gmv DESC) AS rnk FROM g) t WHERE rnk <= 3

questions.question: Find users who ordered from at least 3 different restaurants.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT restaurant_id) AS restaurants FROM food_orders GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT restaurant_id) >= 3

questions.question: What percentage of ordering users placed more than one delivered order?
questions.solution_sql: WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY user_id) SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN n > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_user_pct FROM u

questions.question: For each month show how many users placed their first-ever order in that month.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(first_order, '%Y-%m') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS new_users FROM (SELECT user_id, MIN(order_ts) AS first_order FROM food_orders GROUP BY user_id) t GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(first_order, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY ym

questions.question: Find users who ordered on at least 3 consecutive days.
questions.solution_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, SUBSTR(order_ts, 1, 10) AS od FROM food_orders), r AS (SELECT user_id, od, DATEDIFF(od, '2024-01-01') - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY od) AS grp FROM d) SELECT user_id, MIN(od) AS streak_start, COUNT(*) AS streak_days FROM r GROUP BY user_id, grp HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3

questions.question: Compare the average order value (order_value minus discount) of Pro and non-Pro users on delivered orders.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT u.is_pro, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(AVG(f.order_value - f.discount), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM food_orders f JOIN food_users u ON f.user_id = u.user_id WHERE f.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY u.is_pro

questions.question: For each rider compute the percentage of delivered orders that took more than 45 minutes.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, COUNT(*) AS deliveries, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_minutes > 45 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS sla_breach_pct FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY rider_id ORDER BY sla_breach_pct DESC

questions.question: Show monthly GMV (delivered orders) with the month-over-month growth percentage.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(order_ts, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(order_value - discount) AS gmv FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(order_ts, '%Y-%m')) SELECT ym, gmv, ROUND((gmv - LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY ym)) * 100.0 / LAG(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY ym), 2) AS mom_growth_pct FROM m ORDER BY ym

questions.question: Bucket delivered orders by discount (None, up to 50, above 50) and show order count and average order value per bucket.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN discount = 0 THEN 'None' WHEN discount <= 50 THEN 'Up to 50' ELSE 'Above 50' END AS discount_bucket, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(AVG(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY CASE WHEN discount = 0 THEN 'None' WHEN discount <= 50 THEN 'Up to 50' ELSE 'Above 50' END

questions.question: What share of delivered orders is placed in the lunch window (12:00-14:59) and the dinner window (19:00-22:59)?
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN HOUR(order_ts) BETWEEN 12 AND 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS lunch_pct, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN HOUR(order_ts) BETWEEN 19 AND 22 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS dinner_pct FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered'

questions.question: List restaurants with a listed rating of at least 4.0 whose cancellation rate is below 15 percent.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT r.restaurant_name, r.avg_rating FROM restaurants r WHERE r.avg_rating >= 4.0 AND (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN f.status = 'Cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) FROM food_orders f WHERE f.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id) < 15

questions.question: What percentage of users who ordered in January 2024 ordered again in February 2024?
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT f.user_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM food_orders WHERE order_ts BETWEEN '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2024-01-31 23:59:59'), 2) AS retained_pct FROM food_orders f WHERE f.order_ts BETWEEN '2024-02-01 00:00:00' AND '2024-02-29 23:59:59' AND f.user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM food_orders WHERE order_ts BETWEEN '2024-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2024-01-31 23:59:59')

questions.question: Compute the average number of delivered orders per rider per active day.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT SUBSTR(order_ts, 1, 10)), 2) AS orders_per_active_day FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY rider_id

questions.question: For users with at least two orders, show the number of days between their first and second order.
questions.solution_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT user_id, SUBSTR(order_ts, 1, 10) AS od, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY order_ts) AS rn FROM food_orders) SELECT a.user_id, DATEDIFF(b.od, a.od) AS days_to_second_order FROM r a JOIN r b ON a.user_id = b.user_id AND a.rn = 1 AND b.rn = 2

questions.question: List users whose most recent order was cancelled.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT user_id, order_id, order_ts FROM (SELECT user_id, order_id, order_ts, status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY order_ts DESC) AS rn FROM food_orders) t WHERE rn = 1 AND status = 'Cancelled'

questions.question: Find the restaurant with the best average customer rating among restaurants with at least 10 rated orders.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT r.restaurant_name, COUNT(f.rating) AS rated_orders, ROUND(AVG(f.rating), 2) AS avg_customer_rating FROM food_orders f JOIN restaurants r ON f.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id WHERE f.rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.restaurant_name HAVING COUNT(f.rating) >= 10 ORDER BY avg_customer_rating DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Compare delivered GMV on weekends versus weekdays (MySQL DAYOFWEEK: 1 = Sunday, 7 = Saturday).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_ts) IN (1, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, SUM(order_value - discount) AS gmv, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM food_orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY CASE WHEN DAYOFWEEK(order_ts) IN (1, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END

questions.question: Find restaurants whose listed avg_rating is more than 0.5 higher than the average rating customers actually gave on their orders.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT r.restaurant_name, r.avg_rating AS listed_rating, ROUND(AVG(f.rating), 2) AS actual_rating FROM restaurants r JOIN food_orders f ON r.restaurant_id = f.restaurant_id WHERE f.rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.restaurant_name, r.avg_rating HAVING r.avg_rating - AVG(f.rating) > 0.5

questions.question: For each cuisine show the number of orders and the number of distinct users who ordered it.

questions.question: In each city list the top 2 restaurants by number of delivered orders.

questions.question: Show the 5 users who received the most total discount value on delivered orders.

questions.question: Show the cancellation percentage by time of day: Morning (6-11), Afternoon (12-16), Evening (17-21), Night (otherwise).

questions.question: For every user find the cuisine they ordered most often (one row per user; break ties alphabetically).

questions.question: Find the rider with the highest average customer rating (ignore NULL ratings; at least 15 rated deliveries).

questions.question: Why should monetary values be stored as DECIMAL (or integer paise) rather than FLOAT?
questions.model_answer: FLOAT/DOUBLE are binary approximations, so 0.1 + 0.2 style rounding errors accumulate in sums and reconciliation. DECIMAL(p,s) or integers in the smallest currency unit are exact.

questions.question: How do you make a payment-insert API idempotent at the database layer?
questions.model_answer: Store a client-supplied idempotency key (or payment reference) with a UNIQUE constraint. On retry, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (PostgreSQL) / INSERT IGNORE or ON DUPLICATE KEY (MySQL) returns the original row instead of creating a duplicate.

questions.question: What is a double-entry ledger and why is it used in payment systems?
questions.model_answer: Every movement is recorded as two entries, a debit on one account and an equal credit on another, in an append-only table. Balances are derived or verified from the entries, giving auditability and making it easy to detect inconsistencies (sum of all entries must be zero).

questions.question: Show the success rate of each payment method for every month.

questions.question: Find merchants whose successful monthly volume increased in each of three consecutive months.

questions.question: For each merchant compute the percentage of its paying users who paid it more than once (successful payments).

questions.question: Show daily successful GMV for June 2024 with a cumulative month-to-date total.
questions.solution_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT pay_date, SUM(amount) AS gmv FROM payments WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' AND pay_date BETWEEN '2024-06-01' AND '2024-06-30' GROUP BY pay_date) SELECT pay_date, gmv, SUM(gmv) OVER (ORDER BY pay_date) AS mtd_gmv FROM d ORDER BY pay_date

questions.question: List merchants whose refund rate (REFUNDED payments divided by all payments) is above 5 percent.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT merchant_id, COUNT(*) AS payments, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'REFUNDED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS refund_rate_pct FROM payments GROUP BY merchant_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'REFUNDED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) > 5

questions.question: For every month find the day with the highest successful GMV.
questions.solution_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT pay_date, DATE_FORMAT(pay_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(amount) AS gmv FROM payments WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' GROUP BY pay_date) SELECT ym, pay_date, gmv FROM (SELECT ym, pay_date, gmv, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ym ORDER BY gmv DESC) AS rn FROM d) t WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY ym

questions.question: Find the top spender (by successful amount) in every merchant category.
questions.solution_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT m.category, p.user_id, SUM(p.amount) AS spend FROM payments p JOIN merchants m ON p.merchant_id = m.merchant_id WHERE p.status = 'SUCCESS' GROUP BY m.category, p.user_id) SELECT category, user_id, spend FROM (SELECT category, user_id, spend, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY spend DESC) AS rn FROM s) t WHERE rn = 1

questions.question: Within each merchant category show the percentage mix of payment methods (by number of successful payments).

questions.question: Why must a money transfer be executed inside one transaction?
questions.model_answer: A transfer has two writes (debit one account, credit another). Without atomicity a crash between them loses or creates money. A transaction guarantees both succeed or neither does (Atomicity) and prevents interleaved reads from seeing a half-done transfer (Isolation).

questions.question: What is a covering index?
questions.model_answer: An index that contains every column a query needs, so the engine answers from the index alone without touching the table rows. Example: INDEX (account_id, txn_date) INCLUDE (amount) for a query that filters by account and date and returns amount.

questions.question: Why avoid SELECT * in reporting queries?
questions.model_answer: It fetches unneeded columns (more I/O and network), defeats covering indexes, breaks when the schema changes and can expose sensitive columns. Name the required columns explicitly.

questions.question: A trading system reads a balance then updates it. Which problem can occur at READ COMMITTED and how do you prevent it?
questions.model_answer: A lost update: two sessions read the same balance, both compute a new value and the last write wins. Prevent it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, an atomic UPDATE balance = balance - x, optimistic version checks, or SERIALIZABLE isolation.

questions.question: What is the difference between a clustered index and a heap table?
questions.model_answer: A clustered index stores the table rows physically ordered by the index key, so lookups by that key read the data directly. A heap has no ordering; non-clustered indexes point to row locations. Range scans on the clustered key are fast; inserts at random keys cause page splits.

questions.question: What does the default frame of a window function with ORDER BY mean and why is it risky?
questions.model_answer: It is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so rows with equal ORDER BY values are treated as peers and all included. A running SUM over a date with several trades on that date therefore jumps by the whole group at once. Use ROWS BETWEEN ... for row-by-row behaviour.

questions.question: Find traders who hold a net long position in at least 2 symbols.
questions.solution_sql: WITH p AS (SELECT trader_id, symbol, SUM(CASE WHEN side = 'BUY' THEN quantity ELSE -quantity END) AS net FROM trades GROUP BY trader_id, symbol) SELECT trader_id, COUNT(*) AS long_symbols FROM p WHERE net > 0 GROUP BY trader_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Show each desk's traded notional (quantity x price) and its percentage of the total.
questions.solution_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT t.desk, SUM(tr.quantity * tr.price) AS notional FROM trades tr JOIN traders t ON tr.trader_id = t.trader_id GROUP BY t.desk) SELECT desk, notional, ROUND(notional * 100.0 / SUM(notional) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM d

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Find the largest trade (by notional value) of every desk.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT desk, trade_id, notional FROM (SELECT t.desk, tr.trade_id, tr.quantity * tr.price AS notional, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.desk ORDER BY tr.quantity * tr.price DESC) AS rn FROM trades tr JOIN traders t ON tr.trader_id = t.trader_id) x WHERE rn = 1

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: List symbols that were traded by at least 4 different traders.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT symbol, COUNT(DISTINCT trader_id) AS traders FROM trades GROUP BY symbol HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT trader_id) >= 4

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Show cumulative traded quantity per symbol over trade dates.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT symbol, trade_date, quantity, SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY trade_date, trade_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_qty FROM trades ORDER BY symbol, trade_date, trade_id

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Compute the principal-weighted average interest rate for each loan status.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT status, ROUND(SUM(principal * interest_rate) / SUM(principal), 3) AS weighted_rate FROM loans GROUP BY status

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Calculate the default ratio (defaulted principal divided by total principal) for each customer city.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT c.city, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.status = 'Defaulted' THEN l.principal ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(l.principal), 2) AS default_ratio_pct FROM loans l JOIN bank_customers c ON l.cust_id = c.cust_id GROUP BY c.city

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays

questions.question: Find customers whose total loan principal is more than 10 times their total account balance.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT c.cust_name, l.total_loan, COALESCE(a.total_bal, 0) AS total_balance FROM bank_customers c JOIN (SELECT cust_id, SUM(principal) AS total_loan FROM loans GROUP BY cust_id) l ON c.cust_id = l.cust_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT cust_id, SUM(balance) AS total_bal FROM accounts GROUP BY cust_id) a ON c.cust_id = a.cust_id WHERE l.total_loan > 10 * COALESCE(a.total_bal, 0)

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: For each account find its second highest successful transaction amount (DENSE_RANK), skipping accounts with fewer than two distinct amounts.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT account_id, amount FROM (SELECT account_id, amount, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rnk FROM transactions WHERE status = 'SUCCESS') t WHERE rnk = 2

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: For each branch show the account with the highest balance.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT branch, account_id, balance FROM (SELECT branch, account_id, balance, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY branch ORDER BY balance DESC) AS rn FROM accounts) t WHERE rn = 1

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Find the customer with the highest total balance in every city.
questions.solution_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.city, c.cust_name, SUM(a.balance) AS total FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.cust_id = a.cust_id GROUP BY c.cust_id, c.city, c.cust_name) SELECT city, cust_name, total FROM (SELECT city, cust_name, total, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY total DESC) AS rnk FROM t) x WHERE rnk = 1

questions.company_name: Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays
questions.question: Calculate the monthly EMI of every loan using EMI = P x r x (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1), where r = annual rate / 12 / 100 and n = tenure_months.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT loan_id, principal, ROUND(principal * (interest_rate / 1200.0) * POWER(1 + interest_rate / 1200.0, tenure_months) / (POWER(1 + interest_rate / 1200.0, tenure_months) - 1), 2) AS emi FROM loans

questions.question: Show the completion rate (completed rides divided by all ride requests) for each city.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS requests, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS completion_rate_pct FROM rides GROUP BY city

questions.question: Split cancellations by who cancelled (rider or driver) for each city and show both counts.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT city, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled_Rider' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rider_cancels, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Cancelled_Driver' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS driver_cancels FROM rides GROUP BY city

questions.question: Compute the average fare per kilometre for completed rides in each city.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT city, ROUND(SUM(fare) / SUM(distance_km), 2) AS fare_per_km FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY city

questions.question: For each rider show the date, distance and fare of their first completed ride.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, request_ts, distance_km, fare FROM (SELECT rider_id, request_ts, distance_km, fare, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rider_id ORDER BY request_ts) AS rn FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed') t WHERE rn = 1

questions.question: List drivers whose rating is above the average rating of drivers in the same city.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT d.driver_name, d.city, d.rating FROM drivers d WHERE d.rating > (SELECT AVG(rating) FROM drivers WHERE city = d.city)

questions.question: For each hour of the day show the number of requests and the percentage that ended with No_Driver.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT HOUR(request_ts) AS hr, COUNT(*) AS requests, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'No_Driver' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS no_driver_pct FROM rides GROUP BY HOUR(request_ts) ORDER BY no_driver_pct DESC

questions.question: Find the top 3 earning drivers (completed ride fares) in every city, keeping ties.
questions.solution_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT d.city, d.driver_name, SUM(r.fare) AS earnings FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON r.driver_id = d.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.city, d.driver_name) SELECT city, driver_name, earnings FROM (SELECT city, driver_name, earnings, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY earnings DESC) AS rnk FROM e) t WHERE rnk <= 3

questions.question: Find riders who completed at least 2 rides on the same calendar day.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, SUBSTR(request_ts, 1, 10) AS ride_day, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY rider_id, SUBSTR(request_ts, 1, 10) HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

questions.question: For each driver count the number of distinct days on which they completed at least one ride.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT driver_id, COUNT(DISTINCT SUBSTR(request_ts, 1, 10)) AS active_days FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY driver_id ORDER BY active_days DESC

questions.question: Find completed rides whose fare per kilometre is more than twice the overall average fare per kilometre.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ride_id, distance_km, fare, ROUND(fare / distance_km, 2) AS fare_per_km FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' AND fare / distance_km > 2 * (SELECT SUM(fare) / SUM(distance_km) FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed')

questions.question: Find riders who have more cancelled or unfulfilled requests than completed rides.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed, SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS not_completed FROM rides GROUP BY rider_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

questions.question: Show monthly completed rides and the growth percentage versus the previous month.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(request_ts, '%Y-%m') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(request_ts, '%Y-%m')) SELECT ym, rides, ROUND((rides - LAG(rides) OVER (ORDER BY ym)) * 100.0 / LAG(rides) OVER (ORDER BY ym), 2) AS growth_pct FROM m ORDER BY ym

questions.question: Find rider-driver pairs that completed at least 2 rides together.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT rider_id, driver_id, COUNT(*) AS rides_together FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' GROUP BY rider_id, driver_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY rides_together DESC

questions.question: Show each driver's completed rides with a running count of rides completed so far.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT driver_id, ride_id, request_ts, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY request_ts, ride_id) AS ride_number FROM rides WHERE status = 'Completed' ORDER BY driver_id, request_ts

questions.question: Compare average distance of completed rides with that of rider-cancelled requests.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT status, ROUND(AVG(distance_km), 2) AS avg_km, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides WHERE status IN ('Completed', 'Cancelled_Rider') GROUP BY status

questions.question: Rank brands by return rate (items from Returned orders divided by all items sold), showing only brands with at least 20 items sold.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.brand, COUNT(*) AS items, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'Returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.brand HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC

questions.question: Show the average basket size (items per order) for every payment mode.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT o.payment_mode, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_items_per_order FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.payment_mode

questions.question: Find customers who bought from both the Fashion and the Home categories.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category IN ('Fashion', 'Home') GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = 2

questions.question: Bucket orders by total value (under 2000, 2000-9999, 10000 and above) and show orders and total revenue per bucket.
questions.solution_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS val FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT CASE WHEN val < 2000 THEN 'Under 2000' WHEN val < 10000 THEN '2000-9999' ELSE '10000+' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(val) AS revenue FROM t GROUP BY CASE WHEN val < 2000 THEN 'Under 2000' WHEN val < 10000 THEN '2000-9999' ELSE '10000+' END

questions.question: Compare Prime and non-Prime customers on number of orders per customer.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT c.is_prime, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customers, ROUND(COUNT(o.order_id) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id), 2) AS orders_per_customer FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.is_prime

questions.question: For each category find the month with the largest month-over-month increase in delivered revenue.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT p.category, DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS rev FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY p.category, DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m')), d AS (SELECT category, ym, rev - LAG(rev) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY ym) AS inc FROM m) SELECT category, ym, inc FROM (SELECT category, ym, inc, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY inc DESC) AS rn FROM d WHERE inc IS NOT NULL) t WHERE rn = 1

questions.question: Show the total value of unsold inventory (price x stock) for products that have never been ordered.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT p.product_name, p.price * p.stock AS dead_stock_value FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id)

questions.question: Show the count of reviews for each rating value 1 to 5, including ratings with zero reviews.
questions.solution_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT 1 AS rating UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5) SELECT r.rating, COUNT(rv.review_id) AS reviews FROM r LEFT JOIN reviews rv ON rv.rating = r.rating GROUP BY r.rating ORDER BY r.rating

questions.question: For customers who bought a Fashion item, list the other categories they have also bought from (customer_id and category).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id, p.category FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category <> 'Fashion' AND o.customer_id IN (SELECT o2.customer_id FROM orders o2 JOIN order_items oi2 ON o2.order_id = oi2.order_id JOIN products p2 ON oi2.product_id = p2.product_id WHERE p2.category = 'Fashion')

questions.question: Show each product's price rank within its brand (1 = most expensive) and the difference from the brand's average price.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT brand, product_name, price, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY brand ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank, ROUND(price - AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY brand), 2) AS diff_from_brand_avg FROM products ORDER BY brand, price_rank

questions.question: Find customers who signed up before 2023 but have not ordered anything in 2024.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name FROM customers c WHERE c.signup_date < '2023-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_date >= '2024-01-01')

questions.question: What percentage of delivered revenue comes from customers in the top 3 cities?
questions.solution_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS rev FROM orders o JOIN customers cu ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY cu.city), r AS (SELECT city, rev, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC) AS rn FROM c) SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN rn <= 3 THEN rev ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(rev), 2) AS top3_city_share_pct FROM r

questions.question: Find customers whose order value has increased in each successive order (strictly increasing across all their orders, at least 3 orders).
questions.solution_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS val FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id), l AS (SELECT customer_id, val, LAG(val) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_id) AS prev_val FROM t) SELECT customer_id FROM l GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 AND SUM(CASE WHEN prev_val IS NOT NULL AND val <= prev_val THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Define MRR and ARR and how churn affects them.
questions.model_answer: MRR (monthly recurring revenue) is the sum of normalised monthly fees of active subscriptions; ARR is MRR x 12. Churned MRR is the fee of subscriptions that ended in the period. Net new MRR = new + expansion - contraction - churned.

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: How would you model subscription history so that past plan changes are preserved (SCD Type 2)?
questions.model_answer: Store one row per plan period with start_date, end_date (NULL or 9999-12-31 for current) and an is_current flag. A change closes the old row (set end_date) and inserts a new row. Queries 'as of date D' filter start_date <= D AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > D).

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: How many subscriptions were active on 2024-03-31, and what was the MRR (sum of monthly_fee) by plan on that date?
questions.solution_sql: SELECT plan, COUNT(*) AS active_subs, SUM(monthly_fee) AS mrr FROM subscriptions WHERE start_date <= '2024-03-31' AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > '2024-03-31') GROUP BY plan

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Show MRR at the end of January, February and March 2024 (use a small CTE of month-end dates).
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '2024-01-31' AS d UNION ALL SELECT '2024-02-29' UNION ALL SELECT '2024-03-31') SELECT m.d AS month_end, COALESCE(SUM(s.monthly_fee), 0) AS mrr FROM m LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON s.start_date <= m.d AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > m.d) GROUP BY m.d ORDER BY m.d

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: For each month of 2024 show subscriptions that churned (end_date in that month) and the churn rate versus subscriptions active at the start of the month.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '2024-01-01' AS s, '2024-01-31' AS e UNION ALL SELECT '2024-02-01', '2024-02-29' UNION ALL SELECT '2024-03-01', '2024-03-31' UNION ALL SELECT '2024-04-01', '2024-04-30') SELECT m.s AS month_start, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.end_date BETWEEN m.s AND m.e) AS churned, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.start_date < m.s AND (x.end_date IS NULL OR x.end_date >= m.s)) AS active_at_start FROM m ORDER BY m.s

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Compute ARPU: the average monthly_fee across currently active subscriptions (end_date IS NULL).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(monthly_fee), 2) AS arpu FROM subscriptions WHERE end_date IS NULL

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: For churned subscriptions, find the average lifetime in days for each plan.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT plan, COUNT(*) AS churned_subs, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date)), 1) AS avg_lifetime_days FROM subscriptions WHERE end_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY plan

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Estimate each subscription's revenue to date through 2024-06-30: monthly_fee x months active (use days / 30.4), ending at end_date or 2024-06-30.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT sub_id, user_id, plan, ROUND(monthly_fee * DATEDIFF(COALESCE(end_date, '2024-06-30'), start_date) / 30.4, 2) AS revenue_to_date FROM subscriptions

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Find active subscribers who logged in on fewer than 20 days in the whole period (low-engagement paying users).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT s.user_id, COUNT(l.login_date) AS login_days FROM subscriptions s LEFT JOIN logins l ON l.user_id = s.user_id WHERE s.end_date IS NULL GROUP BY s.user_id HAVING COUNT(l.login_date) < 20

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Show the share of each plan among currently active subscriptions.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT plan, COUNT(*) AS subs, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS share_pct FROM subscriptions WHERE end_date IS NULL GROUP BY plan

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: Find users who started a subscription within 30 days of signing up.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT s.user_id, u.signup_date, s.start_date FROM subscriptions s JOIN app_users u ON s.user_id = u.user_id WHERE DATEDIFF(s.start_date, u.signup_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 30

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: For each subscription start month show how many subscriptions started and how many are still active.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(start_date, '%Y-%m') AS start_month, COUNT(*) AS started, SUM(CASE WHEN end_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS still_active FROM subscriptions GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(start_date, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY start_month

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: What percentage of subscriptions ended within 90 days of starting?
questions.solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN end_date IS NOT NULL AND DATEDIFF(end_date, start_date) <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS early_churn_pct FROM subscriptions

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: For active subscribers show the number of distinct days they logged in during March 2024.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT s.user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT l.login_date) AS login_days FROM subscriptions s LEFT JOIN logins l ON l.user_id = s.user_id AND l.login_date BETWEEN '2024-03-01' AND '2024-03-31' WHERE s.end_date IS NULL GROUP BY s.user_id ORDER BY login_days DESC

questions.company_name: Freshworks and SaaS companies (Zoho, Chargebee, Postman)
questions.question: For January to March 2024 compute new MRR (fees of subscriptions starting that month) and churned MRR (fees of subscriptions ending that month), and the net.
questions.solution_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '2024-01-01' AS s, '2024-01-31' AS e UNION ALL SELECT '2024-02-01', '2024-02-29' UNION ALL SELECT '2024-03-01', '2024-03-31') SELECT m.s AS month_start, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(monthly_fee) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.start_date BETWEEN m.s AND m.e), 0) AS new_mrr, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(monthly_fee) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.end_date BETWEEN m.s AND m.e), 0) AS churned_mrr, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(monthly_fee) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.start_date BETWEEN m.s AND m.e), 0) - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(monthly_fee) FROM subscriptions x WHERE x.end_date BETWEEN m.s AND m.e), 0) AS net_new_mrr FROM m ORDER BY m.s

questions.question: List the sub-languages of SQL with two commands each.
questions.model_answer: DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE. DML: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE. DQL: SELECT. DCL: GRANT, REVOKE. TCL: COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT.

questions.question: What is the difference between aggregate and scalar functions?
questions.model_answer: Aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX) collapse many rows into one value per group. Scalar functions (UPPER, LENGTH, ROUND, COALESCE) operate on each row and return one value per row.

questions.question: Surrogate key versus natural key: trade-offs?
questions.model_answer: A natural key is a real-world attribute (email, PAN) that may change or be reused. A surrogate key is a meaningless generated id (auto-increment, UUID) that is stable and compact. Use surrogate keys as primary keys and add UNIQUE constraints on natural keys.

questions.question: What is a Cartesian product and how does it happen by accident?
questions.model_answer: It pairs every row of one table with every row of the other (m x n rows). It happens when a join condition is missing or incorrect, e.g. FROM a, b without a WHERE linking them.

questions.question: Name the kinds of subqueries.
questions.model_answer: Scalar (one value), row (one row), table (derived table in FROM), and correlated (references the outer query and is re-evaluated per row). They can appear in SELECT, FROM, WHERE or HAVING.

questions.question: What does EXPLAIN show and how do you use it?
questions.model_answer: EXPLAIN displays the execution plan chosen by the optimiser: scan types, index usage, join order and estimated rows or cost. Use it to find full table scans, missing indexes and bad join orders, then re-run after the change.

questions.question: Is COUNT(1) faster than COUNT(*)?
questions.model_answer: No. Modern optimisers treat COUNT(1) and COUNT(*) identically; both count rows. COUNT(column) differs because it skips NULLs.

questions.question: What are orphan records and how are they prevented?
questions.model_answer: Child rows whose parent key no longer exists (e.g. orders for a deleted customer). Prevent them with foreign key constraints, using ON DELETE RESTRICT, CASCADE or SET NULL as appropriate.

questions.question: What is a cursor and why is it usually discouraged?
questions.model_answer: A cursor processes a result set row by row inside procedural code. It is slow compared with set-based SQL because it adds per-row overhead and prevents the optimiser from working on the whole set. Prefer set-based statements and window functions.

questions.question: What is a materialised view?
questions.model_answer: A view whose result is physically stored and refreshed periodically or on demand. It trades storage and staleness for fast reads of expensive aggregations. (PostgreSQL and Oracle support it natively; MySQL does not.)

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: How are JOIN and UNION different?
questions.model_answer: JOIN combines columns from tables horizontally using a condition. UNION stacks result sets vertically; the queries must return the same number of columns with compatible types.

questions.question: Show each employee's name and annual salary (salary x 12) as annual_salary.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_name, salary * 12 AS annual_salary FROM employees

questions.question: List the distinct job titles in the company.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT DISTINCT job_title FROM employees ORDER BY job_title

questions.question: Return the second page of employees ordered by emp_id when each page holds 5 rows.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name FROM employees ORDER BY emp_id LIMIT 5 OFFSET 5

questions.question: List the employees who have a commission.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_name, commission FROM employees WHERE commission IS NOT NULL

questions.question: Find the average of the department-wise average salaries.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT AVG(avg_sal) AS avg_of_dept_avgs FROM (SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id) t

questions.question: List the departments that have at least one project.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects p WHERE p.dept_id = d.dept_id)

questions.question: Find the cities that appear in both employees and students.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT city FROM employees INTERSECT SELECT city FROM students

questions.question: Find the cities where students live but no employee works.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT city FROM students EXCEPT SELECT city FROM employees

questions.question: Count how many employees fall in each salary band: below 80000, 80000 to 149999 and 150000 or more.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'Below 80k' WHEN salary < 150000 THEN '80k-149k' ELSE '150k+' END AS band, COUNT(*) AS employees FROM employees GROUP BY CASE WHEN salary < 80000 THEN 'Below 80k' WHEN salary < 150000 THEN '80k-149k' ELSE '150k+' END

questions.question: Show each employee's initials, e.g. 'VM' for Vikram Mehta.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_name, SUBSTR(emp_name, 1, 1) || SUBSTR(emp_name, INSTR(emp_name, ' ') + 1, 1) AS initials FROM employees

questions.question: Show each email with the domain changed from acme.in to acme.com (do not update the table).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT REPLACE(email, '@acme.in', '@acme.com') AS new_email FROM employees

questions.question: Insert two new departments, (7, 'Legal', 'Delhi') and (8, 'Research', 'Bengaluru'), in one statement.
questions.solution_sql: INSERT INTO departments (dept_id, dept_name, location) VALUES (7, 'Legal', 'Delhi'), (8, 'Research', 'Bengaluru')

questions.question: Raise salaries by 10 percent for department 1 and 5 percent for all other employees using a single UPDATE.
questions.solution_sql: UPDATE employees SET salary = CASE WHEN dept_id = 1 THEN salary * 1.10 ELSE salary * 1.05 END

questions.question: Delete employees hired before 2016.
questions.solution_sql: DELETE FROM employees WHERE hire_date < '2016-01-01'

questions.question: Rename the column city in employees to work_city.
questions.solution_sql: ALTER TABLE employees RENAME COLUMN city TO work_city

questions.question: Create an attendance table (att_id primary key, emp_id foreign key to employees, att_date, status) with a unique pair of emp_id and att_date.
questions.solution_sql: CREATE TABLE attendance (att_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_id INT NOT NULL, att_date DATE NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(10), FOREIGN KEY (emp_id) REFERENCES employees(emp_id), UNIQUE (emp_id, att_date))

questions.question: Create a composite index on employees (dept_id, salary).
questions.solution_sql: CREATE INDEX idx_emp_dept_salary ON employees (dept_id, salary)

questions.question: Show each employee's tenure in whole years as of 2024-06-30.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT emp_name, CAST(DATEDIFF('2024-06-30', hire_date) / 365 AS INTEGER) AS tenure_years FROM employees

questions.question: List all teams ordered by team name.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT team_name, city FROM teams ORDER BY team_name

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: Show the number of matches won by each team, including teams with zero wins.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT t.team_name, COUNT(m.match_id) AS wins FROM teams t LEFT JOIN matches m ON m.winner_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name ORDER BY wins DESC

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: Show total runs scored by each team across all matches.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT t.team_name, SUM(pp.runs) AS total_runs FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id JOIN teams t ON pl.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name ORDER BY total_runs DESC

questions.question: List the top 5 run scorers of the season (player name and total runs).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.player_name, SUM(pp.runs) AS total_runs FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id GROUP BY pl.player_id, pl.player_name ORDER BY total_runs DESC LIMIT 5

questions.question: List all individual innings of 100 runs or more (player name, match id, runs).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.player_name, pp.match_id, pp.runs FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id WHERE pp.runs >= 100

questions.question: Show the average runs per innings for each player role.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.role, ROUND(AVG(pp.runs), 2) AS avg_runs FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id GROUP BY pl.role

questions.question: List the matches that ended with no result.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT match_id, match_date, venue FROM matches WHERE winner_id IS NULL

questions.question: Find the top 3 wicket takers of the season.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT pl.player_name, SUM(pp.wickets) AS wickets FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id GROUP BY pl.player_id, pl.player_name ORDER BY wickets DESC LIMIT 3

questions.topic_group: Joins: inner, outer, self and anti
questions.question: List every match with both team names and the winner's name (show 'No Result' when there is no winner).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT m.match_id, t1.team_name AS team1, t2.team_name AS team2, COALESCE(w.team_name, 'No Result') AS winner FROM matches m JOIN teams t1 ON m.team1_id = t1.team_id JOIN teams t2 ON m.team2_id = t2.team_id LEFT JOIN teams w ON m.winner_id = w.team_id

questions.question: List teams with fewer than 3 wins.
questions.solution_sql: SELECT t.team_name, COUNT(m.match_id) AS wins FROM teams t LEFT JOIN matches m ON m.winner_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name HAVING COUNT(m.match_id) < 3

questions.question: For each match show the player with the most runs (match id, player name, runs).
questions.solution_sql: SELECT match_id, player_name, runs FROM (SELECT pp.match_id, pl.player_name, pp.runs, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pp.match_id ORDER BY pp.runs DESC, pp.player_id) AS rn FROM player_performance pp JOIN players pl ON pp.player_id = pl.player_id) t WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY match_id
